detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:03. The shot begins from <Picture 4>: a close shot of the child's face with the white linen pinafore come up over the lower half of it, only the bright brown eyes and the tousled golden curls showing above the cloth, the grey shawl behind her. The camera is beside the spread shawl, level with a seated child's eye and two long strides from her face, an 85mm lens. The white afternoon sun stands high and a little behind the camera. The camera pushes in on her face across the whole shot, travelling a forearm as the pinafore comes down off her face in both fists, from 00:00 to 00:03. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, a little girl of about five years old, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] Do you mean we are going to die?</d> His mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:03, as the line ends, her chin lifts, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot.
[Shot 2] From 00:03 to 00:08. At 00:03 the shot cuts to a medium two-shot on the shawl, beginning from <Picture 5>: the girl in the pink frock sitting up with her face clear and laughing, the gaunt bearded man crouched beside her looking at her, the bare rock and the shaded boulder behind them both. The camera is on the plateau rock, level with a seated child's eye and four long strides from the shawl, a 50mm lens. The white afternoon sun stands high and a little behind the camera. At the first frame A girl of five in a pink frock sits at the LEFT of CENTRE at three quarters of the frame height with her face turned up and clear, a gaunt bearded man crouches at the RIGHT at four fifths of the frame height looking at her, the shaded boulder fills the TOP RIGHT. The camera pushes in on the two of them across the whole shot, travelling a long stride as her face comes round to his and her mouth opens laughing, from 00:03 to 00:06. At 00:06 his head comes up off his chest, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot.
